transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Acme Platform), Marcos Diaz (Acme SRE), Lena Korhonen (Acme Security), Ethan Wu (Product)

Summary:
Short sync to review this week's pilot reliability incidents (timeouts, intermittent 5xx, rate-limit observations), confirm telemetry gaps, and agree next steps for the dedicated-fallback design and tradeoffs.

Topics:
- Recent timeout bursts during morning traffic window
- 5xx spike correlated to KV cache miss storm?
- Rate limit behavior and retry budgets
- Telemetry gaps (missing request-id traces) and action on logs
- Security/SSO and KMS clarifications for private deployment

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I think we have about 50 minutes, we'll go over the incident replay and then Samir will walk through the proposed config. Priya, you said you'd share traces up front?
[00:13] Priya (Acme): Yeah, I dropped the link into the doc before the call, apologies if it wasn't obvious. The main thing: between 08:40 and 09:10 PST we saw a cluster of timeouts and a handful of 502s. We think it was around our peak onboarding workflow.
[00:26] Samir (Redwood SE): Got it. We pulled the same window — we see a pattern where request latency climbs rapidly and then the Redwood endpoint starts returning 502s after the KV cache misses increased. There's a cascade effect — cache miss -> longer decode -> backlog -> 5xx.
[00:40] Marcos (Acme SRE): I want to call out that our ingress was also doing a TCP retry loop, which probably amplified the load. We saw retries from the client side at ~2x. Might be our side creating duplicate load.
[00:52] Alex: Good to note. That's the classic retry amplification. We'll want to coordinate a retry budget and adaptive backoff.
[01:04] Lena (Security): Separately, can we pause on telemetry? A lot of traces lack consistent request_id, so correlating to our KMS audit entries is messy. We need request-id in both front proxy and Redwood responses.
[01:17] Samir: We can push the request-id passthrough on the API layer; sometimes the header gets dropped by intermediate proxies. Redwood has an env var to preserve 'x-request-id' but if the customer's LB rewrites it, that'll break.
[01:30] Ethan (Product): Quick question: how confident are we that cache misses were the root cause vs just symptomatic?
[01:36] Samir: Fair -- it's hard to be 100% from traces alone. But latency heatmap shows tail latencies spiking exactly when KV hit rate drops below ~70% for the session model state. That matches the moment tokens per request increased by around 3x.
[01:52] Priya: We did a deploy around 08:35 which bumped prompt size for the new flow, so that aligns.
[01:59] Alex: Ok can we enumerate mitigation paths? Samir?
[02:04] Samir: Sure. Short list: 1) Prefix caching tuning — increase prefetch window to reduce misses; 2) Adjust batching policy so long requests don't block short latency-sensitive ones (priority queues); 3) Add a lightweight rate window on our side with token-bucket rejects instead of triggering retries; 4) Failover to smaller quantized variant when queue depth exceeds threshold.
[02:25] Marcos: On token-bucket rejects, we prefer 429s with Retry-After rather than silent queuing that leads to timeouts. But our app doesn't gracefully handle 429s today.
[02:36] Priya: Right, the product team would prefer graceful degradation but we need to know the expected latency and max queue time.
[02:45] Alex: We'll propose a retry-budget pattern: client 2 attempts with exponential backoff + jitter, and server-side adaptive 429 when queue > N. We'll share suggested numbers.
[02:56] Samir: Also recommending changing concurrency limits per client key for the pilot — we can set a per-API-key soft concurrency that reduces head-of-line blocking.
[03:08] Lena: Moving to security items, a few questions — does Redwood Private support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest? And does anything change for audit log retention?
[03:19] Alex: Yes, Private supports bring-your-own-KMS for model state and artifacts. Audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM; retention is configurable in the Private plan. We'll send the SOC2 artifact pack.
[03:32] Lena: We need the specific KMS integration doc and examples of key rotation.
[03:37] Alex: Noted. Action item.
[03:40] [04:00] Samir: Back to performance, I want to show a short slide (screen share) — patterns: a missed prefix causes KV cold read that costs ~20-40ms additional per token on our infra due to cross-shard fetches. If many requests are long, that stacks and you hit the request timeout window.
[04:17] Priya: Could we change timeouts on the client side as a temporary band-aid? We already extended from 30s to 45s which reduced user-visible errors but increased backend queue depth.
[04:29] Samir: Extending timeouts may hide symptoms and make the backlog worse. Prefer to reduce worst-case work per request or fail fast with 429 and graceful fallback.
[04:40] Marcos: When you say 'graceful fallback', do you mean returning a smaller response or a different model variant?
[04:46] Samir: Both. We can fallback to a quantized Llama-like variant or a shorter-output policy (fewer max tokens) depending on client preference.
[04:55] Ethan: Any cost impact numbers for fallback-to-quantized?
[04:58] Alex: Roughly 35-50% per-token cost reduction but with some quality regression. We'll include bench numbers in the follow-up doc.
[05:07] [08:00] Priya: For the spike test — we'll run a 1k concurrent synthetic load routed through our edge and then let it go for 5 minutes. We want Redwood to watch metrics — rps, p50/p95/p99, KV hitrate, queue depth, 5xx count.
[05:25] Samir: Good. We'll also enable more verbose request tracing for that window and keep KV cache warmers running. Please don't forget to include a test that increases prompt length mid-run to emulate the deployment change.
[05:37] Priya: Will do.
[05:40] Marco s: (overlap) Also on our side, we'll disable client-side retry for that run to avoid amplifying load.
[05:46] Samir: Thanks.
[05:50] [12:00] Alex: I want to call out telemetry gaps — we couldn't tie some 502s to a full trace because the front proxy stripped the x-request-id and our trace sampler didn't pick it up.
[12:12] Priya: Yeah the odd thing is our proxy does a header rewrite for tracing. We can change the config to append instead of rewrite.
[12:20] Lena: Please also capture the auth_flow_id in traces so we can match to KMS key rotation events for the compliance audit.
[12:28] Samir: We'll add both request_id and auth_flow_id mapping on our side.
[12:33] Ethan: One more question about rate-limits — we saw a steady 429 tail late afternoon when auth refresh storms hit. Any way to throttle those refreshes?
[12:45] Alex: Two approaches: client-side jittered refresh schedules, or server-side interlock that batches refreshes on a per-account basis. We can help sketch both.
[12:55] Marcos: The account-level batching sounds promising. It would require some client-side changes but would reduce load by deduplicating refresh calls.
[13:03] Samir: For immediate mitigation, we can set a short cooldown and return 429/Retry-After with a small window — prevents everyone from retrying instantly.
[13:15] [20:00] Priya: Anything else on the incident follow-up?
[20:07] Alex: Two main deliverables: 1) action plan for KV-prefetch and batching adjustments (Samir/Alex), 2) spike test coordination (Priya/Marcos). Also Redwood will produce a short playbook for graceful degradation during bursts (failover rules, 429 thresholds, fallback models).
[20:25] Lena: And security artifacts (KMS integration + SOC2 items) to be added to the shared folder.
[20:32] Alex: We'll aim to have the playbook and pilot config by Friday (2026-12-11).
[20:38] Priya: Sounds good.
[20:40] [28:00] Samir: I'll also propose a per-api-key concurrency cap and a default retry budget: client tries = 2, base backoff = 100ms, max backoff = 1s, jitter. Server-side will respond with 429 when client concurrency > 8 or queue depth > 250ms equivalent. These numbers are preliminary.
[28:20] Marcos: We'll review and provide our desired thresholds; our current infra has a hard limit at 32 concurrent but we'd rather smaller soft caps.
[28:33] Priya: For the pilot, can we get a single-day dedicated burst window where Redwood shifts a fraction of capacity to our test lane?
[28:40] Alex: We can schedule a dedicated capacity window for the spike if you want — it's like a reserved pool for the duration. We'll include options and cost in the follow-up.
[28:51] Ethan: Anything about SLA changes if we go dedicated?
[28:54] Alex: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed latency and uptime targets. We'll attach the SLA doc but note that graceful degradation behavior is mostly config-driven, not SLA-bound.
[29:06] [36:00] Lena: Quick question on audit logs: do we get an immutable copy in our own storage for compliance?
[36:08] Alex: Yes, Private can forward logs to your S3 or Splunk with signed delivery. We'll show a sample config.
[36:15] Lena: Great.
[36:18] Samir: Final note — we saw a small number of transcribed placeholders in the traces where model labels got lost; sometimes text says 'model_x' instead of the actual model. We'll improve naming in the next run so telemetry lines up with catalog entries.
[36:34] Priya: That will help.
[36:37] Alex: Ok time check — last 10 minutes for open questions and recap.
[36:44] Priya: One more thing — for the spike test results, can Redwood provide a CSV with per-request latencies and a mapping to request_id? That would really speed root cause analysis.
[36:56] Samir: Yes, we'll provide a sanitized CSV. It will include request_id, model_variant, p50/p95/p99 at the worker, and KV hit/miss flag.
[37:09] Priya: Thanks.
[37:12] Alex: Recap: Alex to share pilot config + playbook by 12/11, Samir to prepare bench numbers and concurrency/retry proposals, Priya/Marcos to run spike test and disable client retries, Lena to collect KMS/SOC2 items and list gaps. Action owners and dates in the doc.
[37:31] Marcos: We'll start the spike on 12/13 and invite Redwood to watch live metrics.
[37:38] Alex: Sounds good. Any objections?
[37:41] (brief silence)
[37:44] Ethan: No objections.
[37:46] Alex: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email and update the shared drive.
[37:51] Priya: Thanks all.
[37:54] [End around 17:22 UTC, 52 minutes total]
